purpose: Make in-memory module interfaces deterministic before graph/interface shadow comparison and importer migration.
question: Which ModuleInterface vector orders are canonical, and which declaration orders must remain source or graph order?
decision: TypeChecker orders module interfaces by moduleId, values/structs/enums by public name, and methods within each struct by method name. Struct fields, enum variants, generic parameters, and graph dependencies preserve their existing source/declaration order.

canonical_orders.methods: ascending method name within each struct
canonical_orders.semantic_sequences: fields, variants, generic parameters, and dependencies retain source/graph order

compatibility_boundary.producer: TypeChecker::buildModuleInterface canonicalizes each module after collecting ModuleSymbols exports and Program graph edges; final buildModuleInterfaces orders the completed module vector and fills only missing records.
compatibility_boundary.emitter: ModuleInterfaceEmitter keeps its existing presentation sorting and output.
compatibility_boundary.semantics: Import visibility, diagnostics, IR, bytecode, artifacts, and Rust VM behavior are unchanged.
compatibility_boundary.persistence: No interface hash, serialized ordering contract, cache key, or artifact field is introduced.

migration: Canonicalize in-memory vectors beside the existing emitter sort, prove stability with differently ordered exports, and retain the emitter copy until all consumers use the canonical object. Later interface consumers can compare vectors without unordered-map traversal noise.
quantitative_gate: The ir_source_location CTest checks module ID ordering and canonical exported value ordering, the m0d-2026-07-22-r1 inventory validates 1,745 cases, and canonical plus legacy parity commands report zero unexplained differences.
old_path_deletion_condition: Remove emitter-side presentation sorting only after every interface consumer relies on canonical vectors and a reviewed output-equivalence gate passes. No other old production path is deleted here.
affected_consumers: interface shadow comparison and future importer migration
out_of_scope: changes to interface text, diagnostics, IR, bytecode, or Rust VM behavior
